provenance: legacy SemStreams capture; not a SemEngine result

queries.question: When quick setup builds the git source from auto-detected project info and the repository has no origin remote, what URL does the entry get, why is '.' never used, and what happens if that fallback also fails?
queries.answer: buildDetectedSources sets URL to resolvableGitURL(info.GitRemote) with Branch "main" and Watch true. resolvableGitURL returns the remote when non-empty, otherwise filepath.Abs("."), the repository's absolute path; never "." because it slugs to an empty system segment so every commit entity is rejected at the publish gate while status looks healthy (audit 2026-07-19, zero git history ingested). If Abs fails it returns "" and buildDetectedSources appends no git source at all.
queries.rationale: resolvableGitURL carries the fallback rule and the reason '.' is forbidden; buildDetectedSources shows that the quick-setup git entry's URL comes from it, the fixed branch/watch values, and that an empty result drops the git source. Neither alone links the detected remote to the written entry and the drop behaviour.

queries.question: If semsource add is run with no arguments on a machine where ffmpeg is not in PATH and the user picks the video source from the menu, what error comes back?
queries.answer: Add lists every registered wizard (unavailable ones labelled "Name — Description (reason)"), then re-checks chosen.Available(); videoWizard.Available returns (false, "ffmpeg not found in PATH") when ffmpegAvailable() is false, so Add returns fmt.Errorf("%s is %s", chosen.Name(), reason), i.e. "Video stream is ffmpeg not found in PATH", before Prompts runs and without writing the config.
queries.rationale: Add supplies the error format and the fact that unavailable wizards remain selectable; videoWizard.Available supplies the reason string that fills it; videoWizard.Name supplies "Video stream". The format, the reason and the name live in different entities, so none alone yields the message; the audio wizard returns the same reason but a different name.

queries.question: In interactive semsource remove, how is each entry in the selection list labelled, and where does the location text for a git source come from?
queries.answer: Remove labels each source "[%d] %s  %s" with the 1-based index, s.Type and truncate(loc, 40), where loc = sourceLocation(s), falling back to strings.Join(s.Paths, ", ") when that is empty; it then prints the header "Remove a source" and calls term.Select("Which source to remove?", labels) to get the 0-based index. For git (and repo) sourceLocation returns s.URL when set, otherwise s.Path.
queries.rationale: Remove shows the label format, the 40-character cap and the Paths fallback; sourceLocation shows that a git source's location is its URL, else its Path. Remove only calls sourceLocation by name, and sourceLocation says nothing about how the list is rendered, so both are required.

queries.question: Does a source added with semsource add image --paths get thumbnail generation set, and how does the interactive Images wizard differ on thumbnails and watch?
queries.answer: parseImageFlags defines only --paths (required, else "image source requires --paths"), --watch (default true) and --max-file-size (default "50MB"), so GenerateThumbnails is left nil. imageWizard.Prompts asks "Max file size" (default 50MB) and "Generate thumbnails?" (default yes) and stores boolPtr(answer) in GenerateThumbnails, and sets Watch: true unconditionally without asking.
queries.rationale: parseImageFlags establishes the complete flag set and hence the absence of a thumbnail flag; imageWizard.Prompts establishes the thumbnail prompt, its default and the forced Watch. Each entity covers one path only, so neither alone answers the comparison.

queries.question: What does Term.Select return when the option list is empty or input reaches EOF, and what does it print when the user types a number outside the valid range?
queries.answer: Select returns 0 immediately when options is empty. Otherwise it prints the bold label and "  N. option" lines, then loops on "Choice [1-N]: "; if readLine reports EOF it returns 0; if the line does not parse with Sscanf "%d" or n is outside 1..N it prints "  Please enter a number between 1 and N." and re-prompts; a valid n returns n-1 (0-based).
queries.rationale: Only Term.Select has the empty-list, EOF and re-prompt behaviour. The lookalike is runSourceMenu's toggle loop in wizard.go, which also Sscanf's a number from the user but prints "Enter a number 1-%d or 'done'." and exits on EOF, 'done' or an empty line rather than returning 0.

queries.question: Which manifest files does the AST wizard's language auto-detection (detectLanguage) look for, where does it look, and what language does each imply?
queries.answer: detectLanguage stats, in the process's current directory (not a given dir), go.mod -> go, package.json -> typescript, Cargo.toml -> rust, pom.xml -> java and build.gradle -> java, returning the first one found (Go map iteration, so unspecified when several exist) or "" when none. It has no python manifests.
queries.rationale: detectLanguage in wizard_ast.go is the only place with this five-entry map checked against the current directory. The lookalike is the manifests map inside DetectProject in detect.go, which takes a dir argument, adds pyproject.toml and requirements.txt -> python and also records ConfigFiles; the ast flag parser's --language help text is another near-miss.
